answer: You add back the entire expense because it is tax-deductible, so it lowers your taxes and saves real cash. Net income falls by the after-tax amount, but you add back the whole non-cash expense on the cash flow statement, so cash goes up by the tax savings. If you only added back the after-tax amount, you would be saying the expense had no effect on taxes or cash.

answer: It is counter-intuitive, but deferred revenue is a liability because we already have the cash and now owe the customer the product or service, so the burden is on us to deliver it. We will also pay taxes and possibly recognize more expenses when we record it as revenue. A liability means less future cash, and that is what deferred revenue implies.
